recipes.name: Newport Clam Chowder
ingredients_raw: 1 pound boiling potatoes, peeled and chopped

steps.text: Melt butter in a large kettle or stock pot over medium heat. Add onions and saute until clear. Stir in flour and cook over low heat, stirring frequently, for 2 to 4 minutes. Set aside to cool.
In a separate pot, bring clams and clam juice to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer for 15 minutes.
In a small saucepan, cover peeled potatoes with water. Bring to a boil and cook until potatoes are tender, about 15 minutes. Drain and set aside.

Slowly pour hot clam stock into butter/flour mixture while stirring constantly. Continue stirring and slowly bring to a boil. Reduce heat and add cooked potatoes. Mix in half and half, salt and pepper and chopped dill. Heat through but do not boil.

raw_recipe.headline: Newport Clam Chowder
raw_recipe.description: "This chowder it is outstanding! It won the chowder cookoff in Newport a few years ago. Try it, I guarantee that it gets rave reviews!"

review.reviewBody:
This was definitely the best clam chowder I have ever made!
My store didn't have fresh clams so I had to use 2 cans of baby clams with the juice, the clam juice was rather expensive so I only bought 1- 8 oz. bottle and substituted 5 cups of chicken broth and it still turned out great!!
Thanks so much for sharing

This was really good! The only change per reviews was I cooked a bit of bacon and added the butter to the fat before tossing in the onions. I assume the cooking time for the clams was for fresh....only canned available to me at the time...so I just heated up the liquid from the canned clams with added bottled clam juice before adding to flour mix. I did add a bit of Old Bay for a kick because we are in Texas and everything kicks. I threw the clams in just before serving and topped with green onions and bacon bits for those who wanted. Very nice addition for seafood night! Thank you, OMMIE3

I made it exactly as written. I used a bit more clams since we had quite a few sea clams. Maybe 16 or so. (These are the large quahog type not steamers ) The natural clam juice is strong already so I added water to about 24 oz of the juice to make the liquid the same. So I had about 48oz liquid. It seemed like a lot of work to use the three pans but it was essential. The potatoes were perfect and not too salty. The roux seemed thick but the onions kind of melted into it. I added the liquid slowly and it came out perfect. I was going to use fat free half and half but we also had regular and honestly just use the regular if you can. The recipe is worth the calories. I used to live in Newport. I believe that this won competitions. It was so good!! In will only use this recipe from now on. One more thing : I used a quarter teaspoon dried dill.

Definitely need to fry up some bacon for this! Chop bacon into bite sized bits and fry up crisply.. use the fat to saute onion and celery along with a reduced amount of butter. I also like a stalk or two of chopped celery. Also, if you are using canned clams, don't boil your clams in the liquid, just reserve them and add them in with the cooked potatoes at the end. Otherwise your clams will be very chewy and rubbery. This recipe assumes the use of fresh clams, which is ideal, but not always practical. Also, there are different kinds of clam species.. most that you buy in the store are best for steamers, but these lack the flavor of clams best used in chowders. Canned clams are generally best for chowders in my experience. I also add a pinch of dill weed, a teaspoon or two of Old Bay and float a pat of butter on top when serving. Yummo! As an ex-Newporter, I can testify that this is the REAL DEAL!!! VERY NICE and thanks for sharing!!

I've made this recipe a few times now and I honestly think this is the Best New England clam chowder I've ever had let alone made. I made it exact to recipe the first time and wowed the Family. 
The second time I made a couple of changes and if possible it came out better. I cooked the clams and potatoes together in the broth and removed the dill and substituted dried thyme, because the family felt the dill was too strong. Now it's perfect!

***Save time AND money!*** Instead of buying fresh clams, buy 6 canned and reserve the juice (since it's packed in clam juice anyway) and buy only 3 bottles of juice. The amount of clam juice in the cans is enough to save you $$ on more. Now, since you decided to use canned clams, you do NOT need to cook these up on the clam juice as they will become rubbery and tough if you do. Also, cook the potatoes in a separate pot ahead of time and you'll be all set to throw everything together. Add 3 slices of bacon and celery if desired. You now have a clam chowder that has TONS more clams and you've saved money on juice. IF you wanted to save more money then I suppose you could cut the clam juice by adding chicken broth and juice just from the canned clams but I have never tried this myself

Wonderful chowder recipe! FIrst time I'd ever made it, and we had some frozen razor clams and used those. Clam juice was almost 3.00 a bottle for 8 ounces, so we used two bottles and then chicken stock for the remaining 32 oz and made sure to put the clam juice from the clams in. I thought it still had great clam flavor. Cooking the potatoes separately is genius; that way they are never underdone or mushy. I also added celery to the onion mix and crumbled bacon at the end, per others' reviews. Rich, creamy, satisfying chowder that got rave reviews, thank you!

I loved this recipe. I took reviewers advice and used four slabs of bacon fat and offset the difference with butter. I used five cans of clams, one bottle of clam juice and the rest was chicken broth. I added the clams when I put in the potatoes. I also added the chopped cooked bacon, and some red pepper and old bay seasoning. My husband and I loved it. I also used four stalks of celery with the chopped onions. This is a keeper.

I was looking for a recipe to make my own clam chowder more delicious. I added a small amount of diced salt pork to the butter and onions. I had already steamed some clams and reserved the broth. I cooked my potatoes in the clam broth . I mixed the butter mixture with the potatoes and broth, added clams and half and half. I did not use the dill. It was the best clam chowder I have ever made!

Good basic recipe. I made it all in one pot by doing butter and onions first till translucent, adding the potatoes and clam juice next till potatoes were cooked through, then the rest later. I also used rice flour (just mix it in before the cream, no need to separate like flour) to make it a gluten free dish and it turned out well.

Having grown up in New England, I've tried a lot of chowders. This recipe is excellent! I crisped up 3 slices of chopped bacon and cooked the onion in the bacon fat instead. I added the cooked bacon back into the chowder at the end. Don't skip the fresh dill weed, it totally makes the dish!

I used this recipe to make Clam Chowder for our local Moose Lodge and it was a hit. Only change we made was that we added bacon. We ended up selling out for that evening. It was a Friday night dinner service during a regional conference so there were a lot of people eating. Very good clam chowder.
I know who this recipe came from, how did they let you have it?!
Terrific! I used 2 ribs of celery and 1 Tbsp fresh dill. And made with freshly shucked clams and juice, but lower fat by using whole milk. Definitely a keeper
Was excellent, I did however use fat free half and half and had it simmer for about 45 minutes to get the watery out of it.
Best "chowda" recipe I have tried in years!

I have a feeling the people giving this bad reviews either are lying or skipped steps. This came out delicious. Followed the recipe but added celery, carrots and corn. Did add some garlic but that’s just our family thing. All three daughters and wife loved it this is a keeper.

I didn't have fresh so I used 2, 8oz cans of baby clams in juice. Recipe has great taste but I added carrots and corn too and did not add the dill. I would put 1/2 cup of flour instead of 3/4 cup. I found it a little to thick and pasty but flavour was good.
Made as written and it was great. One of the best recipes. Made again but sautéed onions with 1/2 cup finely diced salt pork. Also used parsley instead of dill. OMG
